translation_en: Ali—namely, the son of Abu Hashim—narrated to us: He heard Hushaym. Al-‘Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man displayed some merchandise in the market and swore about it that he had been offered a price for it that he had not in fact been offered, in order to entice one of the Muslims to buy it. Then the verse, ‘Indeed, those who exchange Allah’s covenant and their oaths for a small price…’ (3:77), through the end of the verse, was revealed.

Nasr ibn Ali ibn Nasr narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, that two women were sewing in a house—or in a room. One of them came out with an awl driven through the palm of her hand and accused the other. The case was brought before Ibn ‘Abbas. Ibn ‘Abbas said that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘If people were given what they claimed, the lives and property of a people would be lost.’ He told them, ‘Remind her of Allah and recite to her, “Indeed, those who exchange Allah’s covenant…”’ (3:77). They reminded her, and she confessed. Ibn ‘Abbas then said that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘The oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made.’
